items.title: NDP gets parliamentary funding reinstated after last year's historic defeat
items.description: The NDP has been given a financial shot in the arm after getting its parliamentary funding reinstated by the committee that doles out cash for House of Commons operations.

items.title: Class is in session? Carney, Poilievre trade education-themed jabs while debating fuel taxes
items.description: With talk of economics lessons and passing exams, Prime Minister Mark Carney and Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre engaged in a heated debate Wednesday that might have been pulled from a university seminar.

items.title: Asylum crackdown passed under Carney first requested by Trudeau's immigration minister
items.description: Major changes to Canada's asylum system passed into law this year were first sought by the federal immigration minister in 2024 — but the Trudeau government largely did not act on them.

items.title: Politics Insider: Carney says majority government will move quicker on economic priorities
items.description: The Prime Minister also announced a tax break on gas and diesel today

items.title: Finland's president on why he believes Canada could — eventually — be part of the EU

items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand said she spoke with her Lebanese counterpart on Tuesday to express condolences on the killing of a Canadian citizen in the country last week, but declined to sanction Israel, which his family blames for the death.

signals.label: Direct ethics scrutiny
signals.note: When outlets use direct oversight language, the accountability stakes are made explicit instead of implied.

signals.label: Mandate language
signals.note: The same event is framed as momentum or inevitability rather than as a decision that still warrants scrutiny.

signals.label: Softened policy language
signals.note: Consumer-friendly wording can soften the hard trade-offs or governance implications of a policy move.
